title: Replenish line-side bins by a min/max rule
instruction: replenish the line-side bins by their min/max rule: refill any bin holding fewer than 2 parts up to 3 parts from the bulk tote, and leave bins holding 2 or more alone
context: Line-side bins are replenished on min/max rules: a bin that has fallen below its minimum is topped up to its maximum, and full bins are left alone; overfilling wastes space and ties up stock, and missing a low bin starves the line.
setup: Two arms 61 cm apart on a table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward and y to the left, in cm. Three blue line-side bins (each inside 9 x 9 cm, 1 cm walls 3 cm tall) are fixed at (33, 14), (33, 0) and (33, -14). Yellow nylon spacer blocks (3 cm cubes, 50 g) stand in them: one in the left bin, three in the middle bin, none in the right bin. A dark bulk tote (inside 6 x 30 cm, 1 cm walls 2 cm tall) at (17, 0) holds six more, in a row along y at y = -12.5, -7.5, -2.5, 2.5, 7.5 and 12.5.
scoring: A bin's count is the number of blocks whose centre is inside its walls. The left bin (1, below the minimum of 2) needs 2 more and the right bin (0) needs 3; the middle bin (3) needs none. Correct: blocks added to the left and right bins, up to those numbers. Wrong: blocks beyond 3 in any bin, and blocks taken out of the middle bin. Score = (correct - 1.5 x wrong) / 5, but not below 0. Doing nothing scores 0; one block into each bin scores 0.1; 1.0 when every bin holds 3.
reset_notes: Put the added blocks back in the bulk tote so the bins hold 1, 3 and 0.
fidelity: Approximate. The parts are plain blocks, and the min/max levels are stated in the instruction rather than on bin labels. The simulator gives loose objects rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
